headline: Wild’s Joel Eriksson Ek leaves game with injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Wild forward Joel Eriksson Ek left Thursday's game with an injury. Its summary notes he has six goals and 11 assists for 17 points in 20 games this season, and gives no word yet on how long he could be out.

Our numbers show how much his line matters. Eriksson Ek's goals are well below the quality of his chances so far this season: six goals against 11.23 expected goals (a measure of the quality of shots he took), a gap of 5.23. That points to bad finishing luck more than a drop in play, and his 59 percent share of five-on-five expected goals says the Wild control play when he's out there. MIN's share of expected goals climbs about nine points with him on the ice. The Wild are 14-3-4 with a 56.1 percent expected-goals share, helped by goaltending that has saved 14.5 goals above expected, so they can absorb a short absence. A long one would test them.

We have no games without him to go on, so this is a projection based on how the coach has used his players. Blake Coleman (16:19 a night) is next in line for second-line minutes, and Ryan Hartman, busiest on the second power-play unit, is the likeliest to move up.
